concept.name: Hyperparameter
concept.definition: A model or training setting chosen outside the parameter-fitting procedure, such as tree depth, regularization strength, or learning rate.
concept.intuition: It is a learnable mapping or representation used to turn features into predictions or groups.
concept.mechanics: Define a search space, estimate each candidate with training-fold validation, select under a stated objective, and preserve a final untouched test.
concept.failure_modes: Flexible models can fit noise, shift under new regimes, and conceal instability when tuning is repeated on the same validation data.
concept.misconceptions: Greater model complexity or in-sample accuracy does not by itself imply better out-of-sample trading results.
concept.example: Tree depths 2, 4, and 6 are hyperparameter candidates; depth 4 is selected by mean validation log loss.
